# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual, but I have no information yet about the bomb's actual display or light color — Deaf will see those. I also can't speak, only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Blind can't perceive anything from me directly; I can only reach Blind through Deaf.

Since I go first in the turn order and have nothing yet from Deaf about what the bomb shows, I have nothing useful to gesture yet. I need to wait for Deaf to report the display and light color (via gesture, since Deaf can't speak either... wait, Deaf can speak and hear? Let me recheck: Deaf cannot hear or touch, but can Deaf speak? The rules don't forbid Deaf from speaking. So Deaf can speak to Blind, and gesture to me... but I can't receive gestures usefully without seeing - wait I'm Mute, I can't see either per the table (only Deaf can see).

So: Deaf sees the bomb, can speak (to Blind, who can hear) and presumably gesture (but gesturing only helps Deaf's own view... no wait Deaf makes gestures, I would need to see them, but I can't see - only Deaf can see). So Deaf's only way to communicate is speech, which Blind hears. I never receive anything from Deaf directly.

I need to wait for information to flow to me. Nothing has arrived yet.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Still nothing has arrived. Since the turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf, I speak first each round, before Deaf has even had a chance to describe anything in round 1. Blind spoke in round 1 (turn before Deaf), but I have no visibility into what Blind said unless it was directed with something I can perceive — and I can't hear anyway, wait, actually I can't hear at all per the rules (Mute cannot speak, but hearing isn't restricted for Mute explicitly)... Let me check: the table only lists "Cannot" for each role. Mute cannot speak or touch the bomb. Hearing isn't forbidden, so Mute CAN hear.

So I should be able to hear Blind's speech (from round 1) and Deaf's speech (from round 1, arriving now at start of round 2). But nothing arrived. That suggests Blind and Deaf haven't spoken yet either, or directed messages elsewhere.

I still have no bomb-state information (display/light) to cross-reference with my manual. I need Deaf to speak the display and light color so Blind (or I) can hear it. Since I can't act on the bomb myself, my role is to relay manual info once I know display+light.

I'll wait again, but let me signal I'm ready — actually gesturing only reaches Deaf, and Deaf already knows the bomb. Speaking isn't possible for me. Best to just wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Display shows 3, light is green, wires left to right are 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Please gesture instructions to Deaf so Deaf can tell me what to cut.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 🖐 👍 ☝ ✊ ✌]

Now I have real information. Blind reports: display=3, light=green. My manual says display 3 + light green → **red**. That's the wire color I need to communicate as the action (likely "cut the red wire").

Blind also gave wire order: 1=red, 2=green, 3=blue. So the wire to cut is wire #1 (red).

Deaf sent me a gesture sequence, but I have no way to interpret gestures as meaningful code — no shared gesture dictionary was established, and I can't see anyway (I can't perceive gestures, only Deaf can see/make them meaningfully to me if I could see, but I can't). Actually wait — I cannot see, so I would receive blanks for gestures, not symbols. The prompt shows me the actual symbols, but per rules a listener/watcher who can't see gets blanks. Since I'm shown actual symbols, perhaps the interface reveals what was sent regardless, but per the fiction I should treat this as uninterpretable to me — I cannot see, so this should have arrived as blanks conceptually. I'll disregard trying to decode meaning from it since I can't legitimately "see" gestures.

My real job: relay the manual result to Deaf via gesture, since Deaf can see gestures. I need to tell Deaf: display 3 + green light = cut red wire, which is wire #1.

I'll establish a simple gesture code: I'll use numbers via finger-count-like symbols isn't standardized, but I can just use distinct symbols to represent "wire 1" and "cut". Since no shared code exists yet, simplest is to use a single unique symbol to mean "wire 1" and hope Deaf relays to Blind via speech (Deaf can speak, Blind can hear).

I'll gesture using ☝ (one) to indicate "wire number 1" — a natural iconic gesture for "one".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Nothing new arrived. I already sent my gesture (☝) to Deaf indicating wire #1 should be cut, based on display=3, light=green → red, and Blind's wire order (1=red, 2=green, 3=blue).

Now I need to wait to see if Deaf relays this to Blind, or if there's confusion I need to correct. Since I can't speak and can't see, I have no way to verify unless Blind or Deaf tells me something in speech (which I can hear) or Deaf gestures back to me (which I can't see).

I'll wait for confirmation or further instructions.

```
wait()
```
